design.theme: Dark charcoal with named voice lanes
design.scoreOverview: The guided listen shows all 60 seconds on each experiment card. Read the rows as melody, bass and pulse. Each mark spans an actual note.
design.selection: The dashed line marks the guided step. Click a note bar or choose a note from the labeled list. An outline marks the selected note.
design.audition: Hear this note plays its original frequency, duration, gain and waveform through the lab transport.

waveform.fullView: Sample extrema per pixel for the full duration. The trace shows the ideal PCM export for this isolated note.

experiments.name: Repeating melody
experiments.question: When does a note start?
experiments.homework: Change step % 8 to step % 4 in the baseline sketch. Predict the new gap between starts, then play both versions and record what you hear.

stops.label: First note
stops.title: Give the first note a start time
stops.explanation: A slot is a possible start on the score’s clock. Each slot lasts 0.25 seconds. At slot 0, add() calculates 0 × 0.25 and saves 0 as this note’s start time.
stops.listen: Press Play and listen for two separate notes. The first sounds for 0.6 seconds. The empty space after its bar is silence.

stops.label: Same note
stops.title: Watch a slot pass without a new note
stops.explanation: At slot 1 the clock reads 0.25 seconds. The melody rule skips this slot, so the program never calls add() here. The first note keeps its original start time of 0.
stops.listen: Find the dashed marker at 0.25 seconds. It cuts through the first bar. You should hear one continuous tone there.

stops.label: Next note
stops.title: Give the next note its own time
stops.explanation: At slot 8 the rule calls add() again. This call calculates 8 × 0.25 = 2. Each call has its own const time. The first note keeps 0 and the second keeps 2.
stops.listen: Listen again. The second note begins two seconds after the first and sounds higher. Compare the two left edges in the melody row.

experiments.name: Interlocking rhythm
experiments.question: How do three parts fit together?
experiments.homework: Find [0, 3, 6] in the downloaded rhythm sketch and replace it with [0, 4]. Compare where the melody lands against the low pulse.

stops.label: Together
stops.title: Hear three notes start together
stops.explanation: The bass rule asks whether dividing the slot number by 16 leaves zero. Slot 0 passes. The melody and pulse have their own rules, and both also pass here.
stops.listen: Look down the three rows at 0 seconds. The short low pulse ends first. The bass continues after the brighter melody ends.

stops.label: Melody
stops.title: Follow the higher melody note
stops.explanation: At slot 3 the melody gets another turn. Its second pattern entry selects the pitch multiplier 1.25. The code multiplies 262 by 1.25 to get 327.5 Hz.
stops.listen: Listen for the higher melody note at 0.75 seconds. You can see space in the bass and pulse rows when it begins.

stops.label: Pulse
stops.title: Hear the pulse under a held melody
stops.explanation: The % sign gives the remainder after division. At slot 4, 4 % 4 is zero, so this line adds a low pulse. The melody that started at 0.75 seconds lasts until 1.05.
stops.listen: Listen around one second. A short low tap enters just before the melody ends. The two bars overlap for 0.05 seconds.

experiments.name: Four-part composition
experiments.question: How does a minute of music change?
experiments.homework: Try a sine melody in Density in place of triangle. Compare 30–45 seconds. With your partner, record the timestamp and a word for the change you actually hear.

stops.label: Seed
stops.title: Start with room between notes
stops.explanation: Seed is the first 15 seconds. When the slot number divides evenly by 8, this line starts one smooth melody note. Eight slots take two seconds.
stops.listen: Listen for a single part with a long gap after each tone. Keep that spacing in mind as you move to Growth.

stops.label: Growth
stops.title: Hear the rhythm fill in
stops.explanation: At 15 seconds Growth begins. Its melody rule calls for a note every four slots, or once a second. A separate rule adds a short pulse on the same slots.
stops.listen: Listen from 14 seconds. A lone tone opens the clip. At 15 seconds a brighter melody and a low tap enter together. The bass joins at 16 seconds.

stops.label: Density
stops.title: Catch two melody notes overlapping
stops.explanation: In Density the melody can start on four positions in each eight-slot cycle. The notes at 30.75 and 31 seconds start a quarter-second apart. Each lasts 0.3 seconds.
stops.listen: Follow the melody row at 31 seconds. Two bars briefly overlap. Listen for the quick succession of pitches above the low rhythm.

stops.label: Return
stops.title: Hear the final note settle
stops.explanation: Return starts at 45 seconds and leaves more room between notes. At slot 236 this line asks for one final note at 262 Hz. It begins at 59 seconds and lasts one second.
stops.listen: Listen for the bass and melody at 56 seconds. After the higher note at 58 seconds, the last tone drops in pitch and carries the piece to 60 seconds.
